question.problem: If ${X}_{1}∼N(1,3)$ and ${X}_{2}∼N(1,2),$ then what is the distribution of $Y=-{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

However, in this case, we don't know whether ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent. Therefore, we do not have enough information to determine the answer.
